main_text.p: sus[?] est causa meritoria justificationis nostræ, quoniam pretium redemptionis exactè persolvit, & ex rigore justitiæ (ut Theologi loquuntur) pro nostris omnium sceleribus satisfecit. Hæc Car-dinalis; ubi loquitur de solo Christo. Hujus generis instantias alias multas adferemus infrà. Sed hæ jam propositæ hoc consectarium esse subindicant, nemine refragante, nimirum, sa-crilegii se scelere astringere, si quis meritorias virtutes, Christo proprias, sibi vendicaverit.
main_text.head: III. Thesis.

head.i: Per[?] dogma suum de Condigno, Pontificii virtutem excellentiæ meritoriæ Christo propriam usurpant.

main_text.head: SECT. V.
main_text.p: Meritum de Condigno (ex ipsorum Pontificiorum definitione & explicatione superiori) est opus bonum, quod secundùm æqualitatem justitiæ absolutæ, ex ejus dignitate potest[?] premium vitæ æternæ, ex rigore, exigere apud Deum. Tale verò Meritum esse opus ex-cellentia, adeóque Christo Θεανθρώπῳ[?] proprium, rationibus perquam necessariis evincemus, partim in hac, partim in subsequentibus se-ctionibus.
Ratio prima. Opus ex tali justitiæ æqua-litate

page.notes: Top line of the page is a continuation of the previous page's paragraph. "sus[?]" at the start of the first line is partly cut off; "ipsius" is likely but not certain. "Per[?]" in the thesis title looks like "Ter" in the scan; read as "Per". "potest[?]" is a best reading of a blurred word. "Θεανθρώπῳ[?]" is a Greek word in italic, read from a small image; accents are uncertain. Running head is taken as printed, with its "Sect.5." element. No marginal notes on this page.
